kf: Amides (lidocaine, prilocaine, bupivacaine) and esters (tetracaine, benzocaine) **block voltage-gated sodium channels**.
**Adrenaline** gives vasoconstriction: less bleeding, longer action, higher maximum dose.
BNF adult maximum lidocaine (infiltration): **200 mg plain**, **500 mg with adrenaline**; **1% = 10 mg/ml**. Use ideal body weight; reduce in frail, liver or heart failure.
Toxicity: perioral tingling, metallic taste, dizziness, then seizures and arrhythmia: stop, call for help, lipid emulsion.
Allergy to amides is rare; latex and **chlorhexidine** are commoner perioperative allergens.
myths: **"Never use adrenaline on fingers"**: modern evidence supports its use in digits in healthy patients (follow local policy).
patho_lead: Local anaesthetics **block sodium entry**, so nerves can't fire.

mech.t: The un-ionised drug crosses the nerve membrane.
Inside, the ionised form blocks voltage-gated sodium channels.
mech.cap: Local anaesthetic molecules plug sodium channels from inside the nerve, so the impulse stops.

mech.t: Small pain fibres block first, then touch and motor.
Vasoconstriction slows removal, prolonging action and reducing bleeding.
Acidic infected tissue ionises the drug, so it works poorly.

comp: Systemic toxicity, vasovagal faint, allergy (rare), haematoma, nerve injury.
